clinician.final_diagnosis: pathology from a transbronchial biopsy revealed non‐caseating epithelioid granulomas in the alveoli, confirming the diagnosis of pulmonary sarcoidosis.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old man presented with 6 months of worsening shortness of breath, productive cough, and significant weight loss. Initial evaluation revealed respiratory distress, hypoxemia, and abnormal lung sounds. A chest radiograph showed bilateral hilar adenopathy and reticular consolidation (E001). A subsequent CT chest revealed severe traction bronchiectasis, honeycomb pattern cysts, nodules, and mediastinal lymphadenopathy (E002). Bronchoscopy identified a large conglomeration of lymph nodes at station 7 (E004). A transbronchial biopsy confirmed the diagnosis by revealing non-caseating epithelioid granulomas in the alveoli (E004). The patient was started on steroid therapy and showed improvement in symptoms (E005).
